title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Priya Natarajan
content:
Overview

This document outlines Redwood Inference's consolidated policies for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement and purchase order (PO) workflows, contracts and legal intake/approval processes, and revenue recognition/billing practices. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and cross-functional partners (product, engineering, sales, and operations).

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood legal entities and business units.
- Covers: annual operating budget, quarterly forecast updates, capital expenditure (CapEx) requests, procurement of goods and services, contract lifecycle (intake -> signature -> storage), revenue recognition under ASC 606 principles, invoicing, and collections.

Principles
- Control & Compliance: Segregation of duties, documented approvals, and audit trails for all financial commitments.
- Predictability: Budgets should enable predictable spend and capacity planning for engineering and ops.
- Commercial Flexibility: Contracts should be negotiated to enable product and go-to-market agility while protecting company risk appetite.
- Revenue Integrity: Revenue recognition follows accounting standards and aims to reflect transfer of control and payment terms accurately.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Finance (FP&A): Drives budgeting calendar, consolidates forecasts, provides variance analysis, updates revenue models.
- Legal: Reviews and approves contract terms, maintains standard templates, manages signature authority matrix.
- Procurement: Executes POs, maintains vendor master, enforces procurement thresholds and vendor onboarding checks.
- Business Owners (Product/Engineering/Sales): Submit budget requests, forecast updates, contract requests, and justify vendor selection.
- CFO / Head of Legal / VP of Procurement: Final approvers for material commitments as defined in Approval Matrix.

Annual Budgeting & Rolling Forecast Process
1. Timeline
   - Planning kickoff: 4 months before fiscal year start (October).
   - Department submissions: 6 weeks after kickoff.
   - Finance consolidation and review: 3 weeks.
   - Executive review and approval: 2 weeks.
   - Board submission: At least 2 weeks prior to fiscal year start.
2. Deliverables
   - Departmental Budget Packet: narrative, headcount plan, run-rate P&L, CapEx asks, and key initiatives.
   - Consolidated Company Budget: by cost center and function with top-down revenue targets.
3. Forecast Cadence
   - Monthly rolling forecasts with detailed monthly P&L for next 12 months.
   - Quarterly re-forecast at close of each quarter.
4. Variance Management
   - >5% variance on a major cost line or >$100k absolute variance requires a variance memo from the owner.

Approval Matrix (simplified)
- Up to $5k: Manager approval.
- $5k - $50k: Director + Finance approval.
- $50k - $250k: VP + Finance and Legal notification.
- >$250k: CFO approval + Legal review (material contracts).
- Any multi-year commercial commitment: CFO + General Counsel sign-off regardless of amount.

Procurement & Vendor Management
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (required before PO issuance):
  1. Vendor legal name, tax ID, and W-9 (or local equivalent).
  2. Insurance certificates if applicable (GL coverage).
  3. Security questionnaire / SOC2 report for vendors with data access.
  4. Signed Master Services Agreement (MSA) or acceptable purchase terms.
- Tendering / Sourcing: Competitive sourcing required for purchases >$50k unless sole-source documented.
- Purchase Orders (POs): All commitments creating a liability must have a PO. POs are generated through the procurement system and matched to invoices for three-way match (PO, receipt, invoice) where applicable.
- Expense vs Capital: Finance will classify spend at the time of approval. CapEx requests must include depreciation schedule and business justification.

Contract Intake, Review, and Signature
1. Intake
   - Use the Contract Request Form in the Legal intake portal. Include: counterparty name, estimated value, contract term, renewal options, data access requirements, commercial risks, and primary business owner.
2. Legal Review
   - Legal performs risk assessment: IP rights, data/privacy, indemnities, limitation of liability, termination/exit rights, export controls, and insurance.
   - Standard clauses (pre-approved) reduce review time; deviations require escalation to General Counsel.
3. Commercial Approval
   - Sales/Partnerships: Revenue-impacting deals routed through Sales Ops for commission and revenue accounting checks.
   - Product/Engineering: Contracts granting production data access must include security controls and SSO/KMS clauses as required.
4. Signature Authority
   - Delegated signature authority is documented in Attachment A (Legal maintains the live matrix).
   - Contracts exceeding delegated authority must be approved by the CFO and General Counsel.
5. Post-signature
   - Store signed agreements in the central contracts repository (DocuSign + Legal Drive sync). Record key metadata: contract value, renewals, notice periods, owner, and SLAs.

Standard Contracting Timelines (targets)
- Standard MSA with pre-approved terms: Legal review within 3 business days.
- Non-standard or high-risk MSA: 10-15 business days.
- Data access/IRB/security reviews: additional 5 business days.

Revenue Recognition (Summary Policy)
- Policy Objective: Recognize revenue consistent with ASC 606: identify contract(s) with a customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to performance obligations, and recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.
- Common Redwood Scenarios:
  1. Hosted API usage (metered): revenue recognized as tokens are consumed (over time), invoiced monthly or prepaid against credits.
  2. Dedicated / Reserved capacity (term commitments): allocate revenue over the contract term ratably unless distinct deliverables exist.
  3. Private deployments / Professional Services: Professional services are recognized upon completion of the service or over time if customer receives and consumes the benefits concurrently (use contract criteria).
  4. Multi-element arrangements: Use relative standalone selling prices to allocate transaction price.
- Billing & Invoice Timing:
  - Standard hosted invoices: monthly in arrears or prepay subscriptions charged at start of term.
  - Dedicated/Reserved: invoiced per the contract (monthly/quarterly/annual) with proration rules documented.
  - Professional services: milestone invoicing permitted; recognize revenue per ASC 606 guidance.
- Contract modifications: Treated as separate contract if additional goods/services priced commensurately; otherwise treat as modification and reallocate remaining transaction price.

Collections & Billing Policies
- Terms: Standard payment terms are Net 30 unless negotiated. Early payment discounts must be approved by Finance.
- Late payments: Past-due amounts >30 days will trigger collections workflow; >60 days escalated to Sales + Legal for hold/fraud review.
- Credits and Adjustments: Credit memos require documented reason, owner approval, and GL coding.
- Dispute Management: Disputes must be logged in billing system, with temporary hold on collections for disputed amounts while investigation occurs (target resolution: 10 business days).

Controls & Auditability
- Audit Trail: All approvals (budget, PO, contract, invoice) must be recorded in the relevant system with user ID and timestamp.
- Periodic Reviews: Quarterly vendor spend reviews and annual contract compliance audit.
- Segregation of Duties: Requestor, approver, and payment initiator must be distinct individuals for transactions >$50k.

Operational Checklists (Quick Reference)
- Submitting a Contract Request:
  1. Complete Contract Request Form.
  2. Attach SOW and risk call notes.
  3. Assign business owner and expected contract value.
  4. Legal will route for NDA/MSA/Commercial review.
- Raising a PO:
  1. Confirm budget availability with cost center owner.
  2. Complete vendor onboarding checklist.
  3. Create PO in procurement system and obtain required approvals per Approval Matrix.

Escalation Paths
- Budget disputes: FP&A -> Finance Director -> CFO.
- Contract risk beyond pre-approved templates: Legal -> General Counsel -> CEO (if material).
- Unresolved vendor payment issues: AR Lead -> Head of Finance -> CFO.

Appendix A — Example Approval Matrix Table
| Amount Range | Required Approvals | Additional Notes |
|--------------|--------------------|------------------|
| Up to $5k    | Manager            | Standard expense |
| $5k - $50k   | Director + Finance | Competitive sourcing recommended >$25k |
| $50k - $250k | VP + Finance       | Legal notified; SOC2 if vendor handles data |
| >$250k       | CFO + Legal        | Executive commercial review; Board notice if material |

Appendix B — Revenue Recognition Examples (short)
- Example 1: A SaaS customer purchases 1M token credits prepaid. Recognize revenue as tokens are consumed; if nonrefundable and no future obligations, recognize ratably if not tied to usage.
- Example 2: Dedicated cluster reserved for 12 months with fixed monthly fee. Recognize revenue monthly over 12 months.

Change Management & Review Cycle
- This policy is reviewed annually by Finance and Legal. Interim updates can be made for regulatory changes or material accounting standard updates.
